ground_truth_root_cause: The Redis cluster experienced an unplanned primary node failover on redis-02:6379 at 2026-05-16T14:11:14Z, triggered approximately 2 hours after the deploy of SHA 49a7631b1ddb ('Profiling with firepit'). That commit modified redis-proxy/lib/cluster_manager.ex and failover_policy.ex, introducing a regression in the failover election logic that caused extended slot migration (slots 5461-10922) and elevated replication lag on the new primary redis-02-replica-a:6380 (peak lag 8210ms). This caused cart-service to receive MOVED errors, connection timeouts, and ultimately tripped its Redis circuit breaker to OPEN state, resulting in empty cart fallbacks being served for ~4 minutes.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately: page the redis-proxy/infrastructure team to investigate SHA 49a7631b1ddb changes in cluster_manager.ex and failover_policy.ex. 2. Roll back redis-proxy to the previous stable build (pre-49a7631b1ddb) to restore normal failover behavior. 3. If rollback is not immediately possible, manually promote a healthy replica and force slot reassignment via redis-cli CLUSTER FAILOVER TAKEOVER on a stable node. 4. Confirm cart-service circuit breaker returns to CLOSED state and p99 latency returns below 50ms. 5. Post-incident: add failover regression tests to redis-proxy CI pipeline and enforce a minimum replication-lag threshold before promoting replicas.
